METHAMPHETAMINE OR FENTANYL CONTAMINATED PROPERTY DISCLOSURE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814 · Pat Morgan

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Methamphetamine or Fentanyl Contaminated Property Cleanup Act (Health & Safety Code §§ 25400.10-25400.47) as it may apply to the property at 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814, as between Pat Morgan and Jordan Lee. It states what California law provides about the disclosure duties that the chapter imposes once a local health officer has issued an order finding a property contaminated by methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activity, and about when those duties end. It does not determine whether the property at 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814 has ever been the subject of such an order, and it does not tell either Pat Morgan or Jordan Lee what to do about any specific disclosure.

THE METHAMPHETAMINE OR FENTANYL CONTAMINATED PROPERTY CLEANUP ACT
California's Health and Safety Code chapter addressing properties contaminated by illegal drug-manufacturing activity is officially titled the Methamphetamine or Fentanyl Contaminated Property Cleanup Act. In enacting the chapter, the Legislature found that methamphetamine use and production are growing throughout the state and that properties may be contaminated by hazardous chemicals used or produced in methamphetamine manufacture where the contamination has not been remediated. A later amendment added a parallel legislative finding for fentanyl: that fentanyl use and production are also growing throughout the state and that properties may likewise be contaminated by hazardous chemicals used or produced in fentanyl manufacture where the contamination has not been remediated.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "This chapter shall be known, and may be cited as, the “Methamphetamine or Fentanyl Contaminated Property Cleanup Act.”"
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.10(b) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, short title of the chapter (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.10.)
  "Methamphetamine use and production are growing throughout the state. Properties may be contaminated by hazardous chemicals used or produced in the manufacture of methamphetamine where those chemicals remain and where the contamination has not been remediated."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.10(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, legislative finding on methamphetamine contamination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.10.)
  "Fentanyl use and production are growing throughout the state. Properties may be contaminated by hazardous chemicals used or produced in the manufacture of fentanyl where those chemicals remain and where the contamination has not been remediated."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.10(a)(5) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, legislative finding on fentanyl contamination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.10.)
  Known gap: The chapter originally addressed only methamphetamine contamination. The fentanyl-specific legislative finding quoted here, and the fentanyl-specific definitions and disclosure provisions quoted throughout this document, were added by a 2019 amendment (Stats. 2019, Ch. 691, effective January 1, 2020), as reflected in the amendment note appended to the statutory text itself. This document reports the chapter's text as currently in effect and does not independently trace the amendment's legislative history beyond that end-of-section note.

KEY DEFINITIONS: "CONTAMINATED," "PROPERTY," AND "PROPERTY OWNER"
The chapter defines several terms that determine who owes a disclosure duty and what triggers it. "Contaminated" or "contamination" is defined as property polluted by a hazardous chemical related to methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities. "Property" is defined, in relevant part, as a parcel of land, structure, or part of a structure where the manufacture of methamphetamine or fentanyl, or storage of methamphetamine, fentanyl, or a hazardous chemical, occurred. "Property owner" is defined as a person owning property by reason of obtaining it by purchase, exchange, gift, lease, inheritance, or legal action, who is responsible for the property's remediation under the chapter.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "“Contaminated” or “contamination” means property polluted by a hazardous chemical related to methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.11(b) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, definition of "contaminated"/"contamination" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.11.)
  "“Property” means a parcel of land, structure, or part of a structure where the manufacture of methamphetamine or fentanyl or storage of methamphetamine, fentanyl, or a hazardous chemical occurred."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.11(v)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, definition of "property" (parcel/structure) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.11.)
  "“Property owner” means a person owning property by reason of obtaining it by purchase, exchange, gift, lease, inheritance, or legal action, and who is responsible for the remediation of the property pursuant to this chapter."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.11(w)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, definition of "property owner" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.11.)
  Known gap: The statutory definition of "property" extends beyond the parcel/structure definition quoted here to also separately include a mobilehome park, a mobilehome or manufactured home sited in a mobilehome or special occupancy park, and a recreational vehicle sited in such a park -- a distinct statutory paragraph addressed in this document's mobilehome-specific disclosure clause rather than repeated here. The chapter defines roughly two dozen additional terms (such as "authorized contractor," "decontamination," and "local health officer") not reproduced in this document.

LOCAL HEALTH OFFICER'S ORDER AND LIEN FOLLOWING A CONTAMINATION DETERMINATION
Once a local health officer determines that property is contaminated by methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activity, the statute directs the officer, within a specified time, to record a lien against real property with the county recorder and to issue an order, to specified occupants and interested parties, prohibiting the use or occupancy of the contaminated portions of the property. By statute, the order itself must include, among other required contents, a prohibition on the use of the contaminated portions of the property, a description of the measures the property owner is required to take to decontaminate the property, and a statement that a property owner who fails to provide a notice or disclosure required by the chapter is subject to a civil penalty of up to $5,000.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "if the property is real property, record with the county recorder a lien on the property. The lien shall specify all of the following:"
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, lien recorded against contaminated real property (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.22.)
  "Issue to persons specified in subdivisions (d), (e), and (f) an order prohibiting the use or occupancy of the contaminated portions of the property."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(a)(4) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, order prohibiting use or occupancy (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.22.)
  "A prohibition on the use of all or portions of the property that are contaminated."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(g)(6) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, required order content: use prohibition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.22.)
  "A description of the measures the property owner is required to take to decontaminate the property."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(g)(7) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, required order content: decontamination measures (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.22.)
  "A statement that a property owner who fails to provide a notice or disclosure that is required by this chapter is subject to a civil penalty of up to five thousand dollars ($5,000)."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(g)(9) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, required order content: civil penalty statement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.22.)
  Known gap: This clause summarizes selected required contents of the order under Health & Safety Code § 25400.22(g); the statute lists nine categories of required content in that subdivision, and this document quotes three of them (the use prohibition, the decontamination-measures description, and the penalty statement) as illustrative rather than exhaustive. Analogous lien, restraint, and vehicle-license-stop procedures apply where the contaminated property is a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle, addressed by separate statutory paragraphs not independently quoted here.

DUTY TO VACATE A HAZARDOUS ZONE AND TO RETAIN AN AUTHORIZED CONTRACTOR
A property owner who receives such an order, and a person occupying property that is the subject of the order, must immediately vacate the affected unit -- including a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle, as applicable, and any related accessory building or structure -- that the local health officer has determined to be in a hazardous zone. No later than 30 days after receiving the order, the property owner must demonstrate to the local health officer that the property owner has retained an authorized contractor -- a methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory site remediation firm -- to remediate the contamination.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "shall immediately vacate the affected unit, including the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle, as applicable, and any accessory building or structure related thereto, that is determined to be in a hazardous zone by the local health officer."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.25(a) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, duty to vacate a hazardous zone (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.25.)
  "No later than 30 days after receipt of an order issued pursuant to Section 25400.22, the property owner shall demonstrate to the local health officer that the property owner has retained a methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory site remediation firm that is an authorized contractor to remediate the contamination caused by the methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activity."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.25(c) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, 30-day deadline to retain an authorized contractor (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.25.)
  Known gap: This document does not independently verify the training or qualification requirements for an "authorized contractor," which the chapter defines by cross-reference to a separate provision (Health & Safety Code § 25400.40) not fetched or quoted here; only the vacate and 30-day retention duties quoted above were checked against the statutory text.

WHEN THE DISCLOSURE DUTIES APPLY AND HOW THEY END
The buyer, tenant, and mobilehome-specific disclosure duties described in this document apply to a property until the property owner receives notice from a local health officer that the property identified in the order requires no further action. The chapter directs the local health officer to issue that no-further-action determination once the officer determines that property that has been the subject of a preliminary site assessment report has been remediated in accordance with the chapter, or upon a related determination described elsewhere in the chapter.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "Until a property owner subject to Section 25400.25 receives a notice from a local health officer pursuant to Section 25400.27 that the property identified in an order requires no further action, all of the following shall apply to that property:"
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28 (chapeau) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, disclosure duties run until a no-further-action notice is received (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.28.)
  "If a local health officer determines that property that has been the subject of a PSA report has been remediated in accordance with this chapter, or if the local health officer makes the determination specified in paragraph (2) of subdivision (e) of Section 25400.26, the local health officer shall issue a no further action determination."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.27(a) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, issuance of a no-further-action determination (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.27.)
  Known gap: The statute separately describes what the local health officer must do after issuing a no-further-action determination -- including releasing any recorded real-property lien, mobilehome/manufactured-home restraint, or vehicle license stop, within 10 working days -- in a subdivision not independently quoted in this document. This document does not confirm whether any particular property currently has an active order or has received a no-further-action release; that status would need to be confirmed with the local health officer or county recorder for the property in question.

DISCLOSURE DUTY TO A PROSPECTIVE BUYER
Until the no-further-action notice described above is received, and except as otherwise required by the separate Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement provisions of the Civil Code, the statute requires the property owner to notify a prospective buyer in writing of the pending order and to provide the prospective buyer with a copy of it. The statute in turn requires the prospective buyer to acknowledge, in writing, receipt of a copy of the pending order.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "Except as otherwise required in Section 1102.3 or 1102.3a of the Civil Code, the property owner shall notify the prospective buyer in writing of the pending order, and provide the prospective buyer with a copy of the pending order. The prospective buyer shall acknowledge, in writing, the receipt of a copy of the pending order."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(a) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, written disclosure duty to a prospective buyer (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.28.)
  Known gap: Section 25400.28(a) cross-references Civil Code §§ 1102.3 and 1102.3a -- the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement scheme, addressed by a separate document elsewhere in this corpus -- as controlling in the circumstances those sections cover. This document does not independently verify the content of those cross-referenced Civil Code sections beyond what § 25400.28(a) itself states.

DISCLOSURE DUTY TO A PROSPECTIVE TENANT
Until the no-further-action notice described above is received, the statute requires the property owner to provide written notice, to a prospective tenant who has completed an application to rent an affected dwelling unit or other property, of the remediation order, and to provide the prospective tenant with a copy of the order. The statute requires the prospective tenant to acknowledge, in writing, receipt of the notice and pending order before signing a rental agreement, and requires the notice to be attached to the rental agreement. The statute provides that if the property owner does not comply with this requirement, the prospective tenant may void the rental agreement.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "The property owner shall provide written notice to all prospective tenants that have completed an application to rent an affected dwelling unit or other property of the remediation order, and shall provide the prospective tenant with a copy of the order. The prospective tenant shall acknowledge, in writing, the receipt of the notice and pending order before signing a rental agreement. The notice shall be attached to the rental agreement. If the property owner does not comply with this subdivision, the prospective tenant may void the rental agreement."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(b) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, written disclosure duty to a prospective tenant and voidability for noncompliance (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.28.)
  Known gap: Unlike the buyer-disclosure duty in the same section, this tenant-disclosure text does not cross-reference the Civil Code's Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement provisions; this document reports the tenant-disclosure text as the statute states it, without independently checking whether any other statute outside this chapter imposes additional or different tenant-disclosure requirements for the same property.

DISCLOSURE DUTY FOR A MOBILEHOME, MANUFACTURED HOME, OR RECREATIONAL VEHICLE
Where a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle sited in a mobilehome park or special occupancy park is the subject of the local health officer's order, the statute provides that the unit or vehicle may not be sold, rented, or occupied until the seller or lessor -- or the seller's or lessor's agent -- notifies the prospective buyer or tenant, and the owner of the mobilehome park or special occupancy park, in writing, of all methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities that took place in the unit and any remediation performed, and the prospective buyer, tenant, or lessee is provided a copy of the order. The statute provides that if the owner does not comply with these requirements, a prospective tenant may void the rental agreement and a prospective buyer may void the purchase agreement, as applicable.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle shall not be sold, rented, or occupied until the seller or lessor of the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle or the seller’s or lessor’s agent notifies the prospective buyer or tenant, and the owner of the mobilehome park or special occupancy park in which the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle is located, in writing, of all methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities that have taken place in the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle and any remediation of the home or vehicle, the prospective buyer, tenant, or lessee is provided with a copy of the order."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(c)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, disclosure duty for a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.28.)
  "If the owner of a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle specified in paragraph (1) does not comply with the requirements of this subdivision, a prospective tenant may void the rental agreement and a prospective buyer may void the purchase agreement, as applicable."
  — Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(c)(4) (California Legislative Information text), Health and Safety Code, voidability for noncompliance (mobilehome/manufactured home/RV) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25400.28.)
  Known gap: Section 25400.28(c) also addresses, in paragraphs not independently quoted here, the timing of the buyer's written acknowledgment for a mobilehome/manufactured-home/RV sale (paragraph (2)), the requirement that the notice and order be attached to a rental agreement for such a unit (paragraph (3)), and the mobilehome park owner's own remediation authority if the registered owner does not complete remediation as ordered (paragraph (5)). This document addresses the acknowledgment, attachment, and compliance-consequence rules only for the general buyer and tenant disclosure duties described in the two preceding clauses.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
This information sheet regarding disclosure duties under California's Methamphetamine or Fentanyl Contaminated Property Cleanup Act, concerning the property at 123 Main St., Sacramento, CA 95814 as between Pat Morgan and Jordan Lee, states California law as of the date below. It does not constitute legal advice about, and does not resolve, any specific disclosure question concerning the property.

citations.quote: The property owner shall provide written notice to all prospective tenants that have completed an application to rent an affected dwelling unit or other property of the remediation order, and shall provide the prospective tenant with a copy of the order. The prospective tenant shall acknowledge, in writing, the receipt of the notice and pending order before signing a rental agreement. The notice shall be attached to the rental agreement. If the property owner does not comply with this subdivision, the prospective tenant may void the rental agreement.

expectedJSON.gap: Unlike the buyer-disclosure duty in the same section, this tenant-disclosure text does not cross-reference the Civil Code's Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement provisions; this document reports the tenant-disclosure text as the statute states it, without independently checking whether any other statute outside this chapter imposes additional or different tenant-disclosure requirements for the same property.

expectedJSON.body: Where a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle sited in a mobilehome park or special occupancy park is the subject of the local health officer's order, the statute provides that the unit or vehicle may not be sold, rented, or occupied until the seller or lessor -- or the seller's or lessor's agent -- notifies the prospective buyer or tenant, and the owner of the mobilehome park or special occupancy park, in writing, of all methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities that took place in the unit and any remediation performed, and the prospective buyer, tenant, or lessee is provided a copy of the order. The statute provides that if the owner does not comply with these requirements, a prospective tenant may void the rental agreement and a prospective buyer may void the purchase agreement, as applicable.

citations.case: Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(c)(1) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Health and Safety Code, disclosure duty for a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle
citations.quote: the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle shall not be sold, rented, or occupied until the seller or lessor of the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle or the seller’s or lessor’s agent notifies the prospective buyer or tenant, and the owner of the mobilehome park or special occupancy park in which the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle is located, in writing, of all methamphetamine or fentanyl laboratory activities that have taken place in the mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle and any remediation of the home or vehicle, the prospective buyer, tenant, or lessee is provided with a copy of the order.

citations.case: Cal. Health & Safety Code § 25400.28(c)(4) (California Legislative Information text)
citations.cite: Health and Safety Code, voidability for noncompliance (mobilehome/manufactured home/RV)
citations.quote: If the owner of a mobilehome, manufactured home, or recreational vehicle specified in paragraph (1) does not comply with the requirements of this subdivision, a prospective tenant may void the rental agreement and a prospective buyer may void the purchase agreement, as applicable.

expectedJSON.gap: Section 25400.28(c) also addresses, in paragraphs not independently quoted here, the timing of the buyer's written acknowledgment for a mobilehome/manufactured-home/RV sale (paragraph (2)), the requirement that the notice and order be attached to a rental agreement for such a unit (paragraph (3)), and the mobilehome park owner's own remediation authority if the registered owner does not complete remediation as ordered (paragraph (5)). This document addresses the acknowledgment, attachment, and compliance-consequence rules only for the general buyer and tenant disclosure duties described in the two preceding clauses.
